en.title: Writer or Typeface: two enterprise AI platforms, two different jobs
en.metaTitle: Writer vs Typeface (2026): prices, agents, brand control, who it fits
en.description: Writer and Typeface compared: what each does, published prices, agents, brand grounding, hosting and real limits. Checked August 2026 with a clear pick for each buyer.
en.intro: Writer is an enterprise AI platform with its own Palmyra models, a knowledge graph and prebuilt agents for every department. Typeface is an enterprise marketing platform that runs campaigns with brand-grounded agents (Arc Graph, Arc Agents, Arc Spaces, Arc Forge). The deciding question is whether you need company-wide AI or a marketing content supply chain.
glance: Who it is for
Enterprises rolling out governed AI to marketing, sales, support, ops
Large-brand marketing orgs that produce campaign content at scale
What you get
Chat, 100+ prebuilt agents, agent studio, knowledge graph, Palmyra models
Brand graph, marketing agents for research, briefs, content and channel execution, approval spaces, IT customisation layer
Price
Starter $39 per user monthly or $29 annual, max 5 seats; Enterprise custom (third-party, verify)
Not published. Demo and custom contract only
Free plan or trial
14-day Starter trial, no card (third-party, verify)
None shown on typeface.ai
EU hosting
Not published; single-tenant deployment on Enterprise (third-party, verify)
Not published. Site states dedicated models, encryption and access controls
Team features
Playbooks, connectors, SAML SSO, HIPAA BAA, SOC 2 report on Enterprise
Approval workflows in Arc Spaces, governance for IT via Arc Forge
Build your own agents
Yes: 5 custom agents on Starter, unlimited on Enterprise
Configured agents within guardrails; extension via Arc Forge
Named customers
Not listed on pages reached
Asics, Johnson Controls, Sally Beauty, AB InBev, P&G, State Farm

pickA.heading: Pick Writer if…
points: You want one AI platform for many departments, not just marketing.
Model control matters: own models, single-tenant option, external models on Enterprise.
You want a cheap way in. Starter costs $29 to $39 per user for up to five people.

pickB.heading: Pick Typeface if…
points: You are a large consumer brand producing thousands of on-brand assets across channels.
You need approval flows and brand rules built into the content pipeline, with IT able to extend it.
You already run a Google Cloud or Microsoft marketing stack and want agents wired into it.

a: Starter caps are tight: five seats, five playbooks, three connectors, 1 GB knowledge graph. Anything serious needs Enterprise.
Palmyra models sit below the frontier models on general benchmarks, per independent reviews. You trade top capability for control.
b: No public pricing, no self-serve, no trial. Third-party guides disagree on cost (one lists $49 to $99 per user; another says six figures a year). Treat all of them as unverified.
Built for Fortune 500 marketing orgs. A mid-size team will find the sales motion and setup heavy for its size.

en.verdict: Writer wins for a company that wants governed AI everywhere and a low-cost way to start. Typeface wins for a large brand whose problem is campaign volume and brand control across channels. A mid-size DACH marketing team is not the target of either.

bridge.heading: If you want the work done, not a platform to roll out
bridge.text: Both platforms above need a rollout: connectors, playbooks, brand graphs, approvals. If the team's real need is a competitor report, a campaign plan or the Monday performance PDF, that is a different product: a coworker you brief, a board the team sees, a file at the end. Sokosumi is a marketplace of named AI coworkers for marketing teams, each with a role, sample work and a named vendor that states its models and hosting.
points: Brief in plain language or @mention in a channel; the task shows on a shared board and ends with a finished file.
Credits only when a task runs. Free: 250 credits per seat per month, no card. Paid seats €25, €75 or €200 per month.
EU hosting available, stated per coworker. Built by Serviceplan Group with NMKR, Munich.

faq: Typeface does not publish prices. Its site offers a demo only. Third-party guides give conflicting numbers, so ask for a quote and do not rely on them.
Agents announced with the Marketing Orchestration Engine on 4 March 2026. They research, brief, create and optimise campaign content within brand guardrails, with people approving in Arc Spaces.
Does Writer work for marketing only?
No. Writer sells to marketing, sales, support, HR and ops. Marketing is one of many use cases, which is a strength for company-wide rollouts and a weakness if you want a marketing-only tool.
Is there a lighter option for a mid-size marketing team?
Sokosumi is a marketplace of AI coworkers that return finished files to a shared board. It starts free with 250 credits per seat per month and states EU hosting per coworker.
